title: Supreme Court: US Divorce Decree on 'Irretrievable Breakdown' Not Binding Under the Hindu Marriage Act
case_name: Kishorekumar Mohan Kale v. Kashmira Kale
citation: Civil Appeal No. 1342 of 2013; 2026 LiveLaw (SC) 259, decided 15 January 2026
card_summary: A Michigan court dissolved the couple's marriage in 2009 on the ground of irretrievable breakdown, which the Hindu Marriage Act does not recognise. The Supreme Court set aside a Bombay High Court judgment treating this US decree as binding, holding a decree granted on a ground outside the Act is not conclusive here. The bench still used Article 142 to grant a formal divorce after nearly 18 years of separation.
card_tip: A foreign decree obtained only on irretrievable breakdown will not by itself dissolve an HMA marriage in India; the Indian proceeding has to run its own course unless the Supreme Court steps in under Article 142.
verification_notes: The 2009 Michigan decree, the ground of irretrievable breakdown, the Bombay High Court judgment being set aside, the 15 January 2026 order in Civil Appeal No. 1342 of 2013 and the Article 142 divorce are corroborated across Verdictum and The Indian Lawyer reports, with the Supreme Court's own final order (filed 15 January 2026) matching the date.
